selected_mathematical_checks: The atlas deletes endpoints of short pairs, saturates, then marks nonhexagonal cells and d_z>tau² with tau=eta0/L. Each marked location excludes O(L²) surviving centers, and Markov gives O(ND/tau²) marked cells. Hence total loss O(N L^4 D), D=O_alpha(Delta^(1/3)); the buffers include all inserted/deleted locations.

Quantitative actual normal gaps and support distances, not Hausdorff closeness alone, give six near-equilateral Delaunay edges. At each Voronoi vertex at least three cells meet, while four near-120-degree angles cannot. Thus the buffered dual is triangular with degree six. Replacing its triangles by equilateral ones has identity development around each vertex; contractibility of the interior disk removes local rotational and translational holonomy. No conclusion across deleted holes is used.

A segment of length O(La) crosses O(L) fat triangles by the separated-vertex tube count. Across a shared edge, the two near-rotation affine maps agree tangentially, controlling rotation change by O(h+tau). With sufficiently small constants this bounds the gradient by 1/4 from one rotation on the convex disk, giving injection and inner/outer image bounds. This is an actual topology/entrance argument, not an application of FJM before a map exists.

Fixed-disk FJM and Poincare turn the local strain sum into e_p<=C L^-2 sum(d_z+h²). Each vertex appears in O(L²) such disks, cancelling the scale factor in the averaged estimate. Nodal displacement follows from finite-dimensional affine triangle norm equivalence on fat triangles; no Sobolev point evaluation is assumed. Systole at least 100La is retained.

Dividing the stipulated heat comparison by kappa_s and substituting t=1/(4pi alpha) gives w0=1/(2alpha) and ws=pi^(s/2) alpha^(s/2-1)/Gamma(s/2). The zero background and self heat terms cancel before integration. The convergence constants are per finite configuration and torus, not uniform in size or aspect ratio.

Keeping alpha>=T and an arbitrary set of directed positive pair terms yields the cutoff budget delta_s+B_s(T). Splitting the Gaussian into equal halves gives the stated tail factor 2^(s/2), or one for s=0. For pi T d²<=1 the upper incomplete gamma and E1 bounds give the displayed singular costs. Deleting endpoint labels is bounded by the directed incidence count, including any selected nonzero self-images.

Finite subgroup character selection gives sum_x v_mA(z-x)=v_A(z), since N=m² cancels the mean-zero Fourier volume factor. Moving one site changes both its row and column, yielding exactly twice the pair difference divided by N. The regular parts cancel with the stated signs.

The Riesz kernel scales by m^-s; the logarithmic scalar kernel has degree zero but its regular part gains log m. Evenness removes the linear Taylor remainder on the fixed A torus. The exact family therefore has delta0=2/sqrt(N)+O(1/N) for epsilon=exp(-sqrt(N)), and delta_s=2N^(ps-1)+O_s(1/N) for 0<p<1/s, while its minimum separation tends to zero. This refutes all-site uniform separation for near minimizers, not a discarded-mass entrance result.

The variable-domain rigidity theorem explicitly requires curvature/perimeter regularization and enlargement; arbitrary bad-cell sets have no such budget. Finite periodic cutoff estimates and a minimizing stationary-law screening operation do not by themselves give a rate preserving the defects of arbitrary near minimizers.
